description: This comforting Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a cherished staple in Middle Eastern cuisine, offering a warm and hearty embrace. Made with simple, wholesome ingredients, it's a naturally vegan dish that's both nutritious and incredibly flavorful. The bright tang of lemon perfectly complements the earthy lentils, making it a beloved soup for all seasons.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped yellow onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Stir in the rinsed red lentils, ground cumin, and ground turmeric with the cooked onions and garlic. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly, to toast the spices. Pour in the vegetable broth (or water), salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Desired Consistency
instructions.text: Once the lentils are tender, use an immersion blender to partially or fully blend the soup directly in the pot. For a creamy texture, blend until smooth. For a heartier soup with some texture, blend only about half of the soup, leaving some lentils whole. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer batches of the soup to a regular blender and blend until desired consistency, then return to the pot.

instructions.title: Adjust Seasoning and Add Lemon
instructions.text: Return the pot to low heat if you removed it. Stir in the fresh lemon juice. Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning with more salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed. The lemon is crucial for balancing the earthy flavor of the lentils, so do not skip this step.

instructions.title: Prepare Garnish
instructions.text: While the soup is simmering or after blending, chop fresh cilantro or parsley for garnish. You may also prepare some toasted pita bread or additional lemon wedges for serving.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas) into bowls. Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil, if desired, and garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve immediately with lemon wedges and toasted pita bread on the side for dipping.

tips: For an authentic Middle Eastern touch, consider a 'ta'leeyah' or garlic-cilantro sizzle. In a small pan, heat a tablespoon of olive oil, add minced garlic and fresh cilantro, and cook briefly until fragrant. Stir this into the soup just before serving.

If you prefer a thicker soup, you can reduce the amount of broth slightly. For a thinner soup, add more hot broth until you reach your desired consistency. Always adjust seasoning after adding more liquid.

Leftover Adas soup stores beautifully in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or broth if it has thickened too much.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East with a bowl of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, affectionately known as Adas. This comforting, nutritious, and incredibly flavorful soup is a staple in Lebanese households, cherished for its simplicity and heartwarming qualities. Whether you're seeking a wholesome meal, a satisfying starter, or a taste of authentic Lebanese cuisine, Adas delivers on all fronts. Packed with plant-based protein, fiber, and vibrant flavors, this soup is a testament to how humble ingredients can create something truly extraordinary.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas?

Adas, simply meaning "lentils" in Arabic, refers to a category of lentil-based dishes, but none is quite as universally beloved as the vibrant Lebanese Red Lentil Soup. This iconic soup stands out with its signature sunny yellow-orange hue, silky smooth texture (though some prefer it slightly chunky), and a bright, zesty finish from fresh lemon juice. Unlike some heavier stews, Adas is wonderfully light yet deeply satisfying, making it perfect for any season.

At its core, Adas is a vegetarian (and often vegan) masterpiece, relying on the natural goodness of red lentils, aromatic vegetables like onions and garlic, and a crucial blend of spices, primarily cumin. It's a dish that embodies the spirit of Lebanese hospitality – simple ingredients transformed into a dish that nourishes both body and soul. For many, it evokes memories of home-cooked meals, especially during the colder months or as a customary dish during the holy month of Ramadan to break the fast. Its widespread popularity across the Middle East means you'll find variations, but the Lebanese version is particularly known for its clean, refreshing, and distinctly lemony profile.

## Ingredients You Need for Adas Soup

Creating this delightful Lebanese Red Lentil Soup requires a handful of readily available ingredients. The beauty lies in their quality and how they come together.

*   **Red Lentils (Split):** The star of the show. Split red lentils cook quickly and break down easily, contributing to the soup's creamy texture. Ensure they are well-rinsed.
*   **Olive Oil:** A cornerstone of Lebanese cooking, used for sautéing and as a finishing drizzle.
*   **Onion:** One medium yellow onion, finely chopped, forms the aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** Several cloves, minced, for depth of flavor.
*   **Carrots:** One medium carrot, finely diced, adds a touch of sweetness and body, though some traditional recipes omit it.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** High-quality vegetable broth will enhance the flavor, but water works perfectly well, especially if you want the lentil flavor to shine.
*   **Cumin:** Ground cumin is non-negotiable. It provides the essential earthy, warm spice that defines Adas.
*   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To taste, enhancing all the other flavors.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** This is the secret weapon! Added at the end, it brightens the entire soup with its essential tang.
*   **Optional Garnishes:** Fresh cilantro or parsley, extra virgin olive oil, a sprinkle of paprika or sumac, and toasted pita bread for serving.

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Making Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process that yields incredibly rewarding results. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing your red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch, which can cause cloudiness. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, being careful not to brown them too much. Add the minced garlic and diced carrots (if using), and cook for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
3.  **Combine and Simmer:** Stir in the rinsed lentils and 1-2 teaspoons of ground cumin into the pot, cooking for about 1 minute until the cumin is fragrant. Pour in 6-8 cups of vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil.
4.  **Cook the Lentils:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot partially, and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down, thickening the soup. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend (Optional):** For a smoother soup, use an immersion blender directly in the pot to blend until your desired consistency is reached. Alternatively, carefully transfer portions of the soup to a regular blender (vent the lid!) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. If you prefer a more rustic, chunky soup, you can skip this step or just mash some of the lentils with the back of a spoon.
6.  **Season and Finish:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the fresh lemon juice, starting with 1/4 cup and adding more to taste. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust any seasonings as needed – more lemon, salt, or cumin can make a big difference.

## Pro Tips for the Best Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Achieving that perfect, authentic taste in your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is all about attention to detail. Here are some pro tips:

*   **Don't Skip the Rinse:** Rinsing lentils is crucial. It not only cleans them but also helps prevent the soup from becoming overly foamy or cloudy.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice is Key:** This cannot be stressed enough. Bottled lemon juice simply won't deliver the vibrant, fresh tang that defines a truly great Adas. Add it at the very end to preserve its bright flavor.
*   **Cumin is Your Friend:** Cumin is the dominant spice in this soup. Don't be shy with it, but also taste as you go. It provides that essential earthy, warm backbone.
*   **Sautéing Builds Flavor:** Taking the time to properly sauté the onions, garlic, and carrots until they are fragrant and softened creates a rich flavor base for the entire soup.
*   **Adjust Consistency to Your Liking:** If the soup is too thick after cooking and blending, simply add a bit more hot broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency. If it's too thin, let it simmer uncovered for a few more minutes to reduce.
*   **Taste, Taste, Taste:** Before serving, always taste and adjust the salt, pepper, and lemon juice. These final tweaks are what elevate a good soup to a great one.

## Serving Suggestions for Adas

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is wonderfully versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways, whether as a light main course or a flavorful appetizer.

*   **Classic Garnish:** A drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro or parsley is the most traditional and simplest way to serve Adas. Some also like a dusting of paprika or sumac for color and a subtle extra layer of flavor.
*   **With Bread:** Serve alongside warm, toasted pita bread, often brushed with olive oil and sprinkled with za'atar. Crusty French bread or a simple rustic loaf also makes an excellent accompaniment for dipping.
*   **As a Light Meal:** A bowl of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is hearty enough to be a satisfying light lunch or dinner on its own, especially when paired with some bread.
*   **Alongside a Salad:** For a more complete meal, serve Adas with a crisp Middle Eastern side salad, such as a simple cucumber and tomato salad dressed with lemon and olive oil, or a refreshing tabbouleh.
*   **Add a Kick:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a pinch of red pepper flakes or a dash of hot sauce can be added to individual servings.

## Variations and Substitutions for Red Lentil Soup

While the traditional Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, there are many ways to adapt it to your preference or what you have on hand.

*   **Vegetable Boost:** Feel free to add other finely diced vegetables like celery, potatoes, or sweet potatoes for extra nutrients and body. Spinach or kale can be stirred in during the last few minutes of cooking for a burst of green.
*   **Spice It Up:** A pinch of turmeric can be added along with the cumin for an extra layer of earthy flavor and a deeper golden color. A tiny dash of cayenne pepper can introduce a subtle heat. Some regional variations might include a pinch of dried mint.
*   **Herbal Additions:** Beyond cilantro and parsley, fresh mint or dill can offer a different aromatic profile.
*   **Broth Choice:** While vegetable broth keeps it vegan, you can certainly use chicken broth for a richer, more savory flavor if you don't need it to be strictly plant-based.
*   **Protein Punch:** Although not traditional, some enjoy adding a handful of tiny pasta (like orzo or vermicelli) during the last 10 minutes of cooking, or even small pieces of cooked chicken for a heartier meal.
*   **Texture Play:** Experiment with how much you blend the soup. A completely smooth soup is elegant, while a partially blended or chunky version offers more textural interest.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is more than just a meal; it’s a warm embrace in a bowl, a testament to the power of simple, wholesome ingredients. Easy to make, incredibly nutritious, and bursting with authentic Middle Eastern flavors, it's a dish that will undoubtedly earn a permanent spot in your culinary repertoire. Give this Lebanese Red Lentil Soup a try, and discover the comforting magic of Adas for yourself.
